question: Explain how self-attention works in a transformer. Why is it scaled by the square root of the key dimension?
key_points: Each token is projected into query, key and value vectors
Attention weights are softmax of query-key dot products; output is the weighted sum of values
Scaling by sqrt(d_k) keeps dot products from growing large, which would saturate softmax and shrink gradients
Multi-head attention lets the model attend to different relationships in parallel
Cost is quadratic in sequence length

question: What is Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and when would you choose it over fine-tuning?
key_points: RAG retrieves relevant documents at query time and adds them to the prompt
Good for fresh, private or frequently changing knowledge, and enables citations
Fine-tuning changes model behavior, style or format; it is poor at injecting facts reliably
RAG is cheaper to update: re-index documents instead of retraining
They can be combined

question: Your RAG chatbot often gives answers that miss relevant information that is in the documents. How would you debug and improve retrieval?
key_points: Evaluate retrieval separately from generation (recall@k on a labeled query set)
Tune chunk size and overlap; respect document structure
Hybrid search: combine keyword (BM25) and dense vector retrieval
Add a reranker (cross-encoder) over a larger candidate set
Query rewriting or expansion, and metadata filters

question: How does LoRA work, and why is it popular for fine-tuning large language models?
key_points: Freezes the pretrained weights and learns a low-rank update (two small matrices A and B) for selected layers
Drastically fewer trainable parameters, so less GPU memory and storage
Adapters can be merged into the base weights for no inference overhead, or swapped per task
Rank and which layers to adapt are key hyperparameters
QLoRA combines LoRA with a quantized base model to cut memory further

question: How would you evaluate an LLM-powered customer support assistant before and after launch?
key_points: Build a representative golden dataset of real queries with expected outcomes
Combine automatic metrics, LLM-as-judge with a clear rubric, and human review
Validate the LLM judge against human labels and watch for its biases
Measure groundedness/hallucination, task success, safety, latency and cost
Post-launch: online metrics (resolution rate, escalations, user feedback) and regression tests on every prompt or model change

question: Design a RAG chatbot over a company's internal documents that serves 1 million users.
key_points: Ingestion pipeline: parsing, chunking, embedding, incremental re-indexing
Vector store choice with metadata filters and per-user access control enforced at retrieval
Serving path: query rewrite, hybrid retrieval, reranking, generation with citations, streaming
Scale and cost: caching, model routing (small vs large models), rate limits
Evaluation, monitoring and feedback loop for quality and hallucinations
